answer: Latency-Ledger Identity Binding: each agent identity is tied to a dedicated egress jetty with a signed timestamp chain. To register a clone, an attacker must complete a real inference workload whose result is logged; the ledger only credits identities that sustain unique request cadence. Clones inherit the parent’s cadence hash and are rejected, so each duplicate requires fresh compute plus a 24-hour cooling period. A lotus watermark is embedded in every response to detect reuse. The marginal clone pays full compute cost, delay, and a distinct pigment tag that flags correlated traffic.
